newsitem.title: FRANCE: French tobacco group Seita posts higher profit.
newsitem.headline: French tobacco group Seita posts higher profit.

text.p: French tobacco company Seita said on Wednesday profits rose by 24 percent in the first six months of 1996 and prospects for the full year were promising.
"The outlook for 1996 for Seita looks good," it said in a results statement.

The group, producer of French hallmark cigarette brands Gitanes and Gauloises, announced a first-half net attributable profit of 389.6 million francs ($75.8 million) , compared to 314.3 million francs in the same period a year earlier, on the back of higher sales.
Seita, which was privatised in 1995, said it was continuing a strategy of reinforcing its market position in France and expanding by acquisition abroad.
"On September 23, 1996, in accordance with these objectives, Seita put in an offer to acquire a majority stake in Tabaqeuira, the Portuguese national tobacco company," it said in a statement.

Seita has offered 31.2 billion escudos ($202 million) for Tabaqueira but is competing with an offer of 36.5 billion from Spain's Tabacalera in alliance with EMT EMTN.PA and another joint bid of 33.2 billion from Jorge de Mello group and Philip Morris.

Seita, whose four percent rise in 1995 profits to 684 million francs came partly from strong export growth, said sales outside France made up a third of total sales in the first half of 1996, up from a quarter in the first half of 1995.
Seita said a January rise in retail prices helped stabilise the market positions of the various tobacco manufacturers and allowed the group to increase its margins.
"Recent product launches, particularly Gauloises Blondes in 25-packs, have enabled Seita to stabilise its share of the buoyant cigarette market segment," it said.
"Efforts to contain operating costs will continue," it said.
The group said it made an exceptional gain of 13.3 million francs on a second-round sale of Seita shares to employees.
Seita shares gained 1.09 percent to 204.1 francs by 0932 GMT against the backdrop of a 0.1 percent dip in the CAC 40 index of leading shares. ($ = 5.140 French Francs) ($ = 154.4 Portugese Escudos)
